name: Danaher Pin Escape Fundamentals System
description: Explore Danaher Pin Escape Fundamentals System with a matched BJJ Fanatics course, practical study steps, partner drills, and connected technique references.
summary: The Danaher Pin Escape Fundamentals System is a study framework for connecting basic escape movements to the specific control that keeps a pin in place.
overview:
Knowing a bridge or a hip escape is different from recognising when that movement can change a pin. This guide connects those movement skills to an opponent's actual controls. John Danaher's Pin Escapes and Turtle Escapes course is the selected foundational companion, covering general escape concepts before positional applications. Work from one familiar pin at a time; the broad syllabus is useful as a reference, but studying every escape at once makes it difficult to tell which adjustment improved a particular round.

The sequence and drills below are original BJJGraph study suggestions, not a course transcript or an official instructor curriculum. Use the linked demonstrations for technical detail, then compare one selected lesson with a controlled partner round.
key_principles: Begin under side control or mount and describe what prevents your shoulders or hips from moving.
Practise the relevant bridge, hip movement or turn without resistance and with comfortable alignment.
Study the positional lesson that restores a useful elbow or knee connection instead of pushing at every available surface.
Let the partner block the first escape and return to a supported second option from the same starting pin.
Continue beyond the initial space-making action to see whether you have established guard or another stable endpoint.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Performing a memorised movement against the wrong control
common_obstacles.solution: Identify the blocked body segment before repeating the movement.

common_obstacles.solution: Return to the demonstrated frame and movement relationship.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Stopping the drill as soon as a gap appears
common_obstacles.solution: Give the top partner one controlled attempt to follow and repin.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Testing every escape in one round
common_obstacles.solution: Choose one pin and one defensive reaction so the result can inform the next repetition.

training_methodology.drilling_approach: BJJGraph practice suggestion: start from Side Control and give the partner one agreed response. Work through the first two stages cooperatively, then stop each repetition at the chosen control or recovery endpoint. Add another reaction only when both partners can explain what changed. Keep submission entries controlled and release immediately on a tap or request to stop. Review the lost connection before adding speed.
